about: Kudzu is the oscuro blend that launched Southern Draw in 2014, rolled for the company by AJ Fernandez in Esteli. It is a box-pressed cigar with an Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over an Ometepe binder.
notes: Filler: the maker lists Nicaragua and USA; Neptune and Cigar Coop list Nicaraguan only. Strength varies by source: Neptune says Full, Holt's Medium-Full, a Blind Man's Puff panel medium-strong, and a review quoted on the maker's page Medium+. Kudzu Lustrum is a separate limited blend.

about: Firethorn is Southern Draw's Habano Rosado blend and the company's second line after Kudzu. It pairs an Ecuadorian rosado wrapper with a Mexican San Andres binder and Nicaraguan filler, made at AJ Fernandez's factory.

about: Crook of the Crown is the debut blend from Stolen Throne, the Virginia boutique brand founded by Lee Marsh and JR Cannon, released in 2019. It is a San Andrés maduro made with Noel Rojas in Esteli, Nicaragua.
notes: Strength: Atlantic Cigar lists medium to full and Luxury Cigar Club medium plus; a Blind Man's Puff panel and other reviews rated it medium. Filler: the maker lists Nicaraguan; Blind Man's Puff and Luxury Cigar Club list Indonesian and Nicaraguan. Older reviews name other factories tied to blender Noel Rojas.

about: 3 Kingdoms is the third regular blend from Stolen Throne, released in late 2021 and made at the Rojas Cigar Factory in Nicaragua. It is the brand's full-strength cigar, with a Habano Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos.

about: Call to Arms is the second regular blend from Stolen Throne, a Sumatra-wrapped cigar over Nicaraguan binder and filler made at the Rojas Cigar Factory in Nicaragua.
notes: The maker lists the wrapper only as Sumatran. Luxury Cigar Club says Ecuadorian Sumatra, but no maker or top-tier source confirms the growing country, so wrapper origin is left blank. No source gives a firm release year; it followed Crook of the Crown and was being reviewed by March 2021.

about: Skull Breaker is a Connecticut Broadleaf belicoso in the Surrogates line, blended by Pete Johnson of Tatuaje and rolled by the Garcia family at My Father Cigars in Nicaragua. It is one of the two original Surrogates cigars.
notes: Each Surrogates name is a single size. The line began as a New Havana Cigars house brand, moved to L'Atelier Imports in 2012, and is now sold under Tatuaje, whose own site does not list it. Body is disputed: Cigar Coop rated it medium while Cigar Dojo called it full bodied, so body is left blank.
